title: Thrill Ride
summary: Build a roller coaster whose track is the antiderivative: integrate by parts so the rails fit every pylon and the car stays on.
subject: mathematics
concepts: Choosing u: log, inverse trig, algebra, trig, exp
Integrals of log x and tan⁻¹ x
The pattern ∫ eˣ[f(x) + f′(x)] dx = eˣ f(x) + C
Cyclic integrals such as ∫ eˣ sin x dx
learningOutcome: The student can integrate products by parts, choose u well, repeat the method, spot the eˣ[f + f′] pattern and solve cyclic integrals such as ∫ eˣ sin x dx.

levels.title: x times a wave
levels.adds: Baseline: ∫ u dv = uv − ∫ v du with u = x, so ∫ x sin x dx = −x cos x + sin x + C (Ex 7.6 Q1, Q2, Q12; Example 17).
hints: Take u = x, because its derivative is simpler, and dv = the wave.
∫ x sin x dx = x(−cos x) − ∫ (−cos x) dx.
For sin 2x, the integral of the wave brings a factor 1/2, and the second integral another 1/2.

levels.title: Twice by parts
levels.adds: New: exponentials, and x² needs the method twice: ∫ x² eˣ dx = eˣ(x² − 2x + 2) + C (Ex 7.6 Q3; Example 19).
hints: Keep u the power of x and dv the exponential.
After one step, ∫ x² eˣ dx = x² eˣ − 2∫ x eˣ dx: do it again.
For e^(2x) each integration brings a factor 1/2.

levels.title: Log and inverse trig
levels.adds: New: take u = log x or tan⁻¹ x and dv = dx or x dx, as in ∫ log x dx = x log x − x + C (Ex 7.6 Q4 to Q9, Q13; Example 18).
hints: Log and inverse trigonometric functions have easy derivatives, so make them u.
∫ log x dx: u = log x, dv = dx, so v = x.
∫ tan⁻¹ x dx = x tan⁻¹ x − ∫ x/(1 + x²) dx, and the last part is (1/2) log(1 + x²).

levels.title: The eˣ pattern
levels.adds: New: when the integrand is eˣ[f(x) + f′(x)], the answer is eˣ f(x) + C; find f (Ex 7.6 Q16 to Q20; Example 22).
hints: Split the bracket into a function and its own derivative.
eˣ(sin x + cos x): f = sin x, since (sin x)′ = cos x.

levels.title: Round and round
levels.adds: New: cyclic integrals. By parts twice brings the integral back, so solve for it: ∫ eˣ sin x dx = ½eˣ(sin x − cos x) + C (Ex 7.6 Q21; Example 21).
hints: Call the integral I and integrate by parts twice, keeping the same choice of u.
The integral you started with comes back: I = (something) − I.

misconceptions: ∫ uv dx = ∫ u dx · ∫ v dx
The choice of u does not matter
A cyclic integral by parts goes round forever and cannot be solved
